$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `governance`'s canonical store, the
SIXTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM. One
entry per guard: per scope predicate, per vocabulary check that stands where
no enum stands, per shape check that stands where a migration-only CHECK
stands, per envelope decision that keeps a row an older binary wrote
readable, and per statement the port's contract says must be one statement.
Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements it
(`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were seen
to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A SEVENTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json and mutations-cost.json rather than an extension of any
of them, for the reason the fourth was: seven tranches are seven separate
claims about seven separate port surfaces, and a reader checking one should
not have to read past the other six. All are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. Three of its guards protect facts the
DATABASE does not hold at all. `SafetyEvent.detector`, `.action` and
`.severity` are plain `String` columns — the closed sets live only in
`domain/safety-event.ts` — so a store that CAST them would put a value
outside the union into `summarise`, whose histograms are keyed by the union,
and the total would stop equalling the sum of the parts with no error
anywhere. And three fields of `AdmittedSafetyEvent` have no column, so they
ride in a discriminated envelope inside `metadata`: an envelope that stopped
discriminating would read a detector's own `principalId` attribute as the
ledger's subject, and erase somebody else's rows on the strength of it.
None of the three is visible in a returned value on a store with one caller.
AND ONE GUARD REFUSES A VALUE THE DOMAIN CONSIDERS VALID.
`MessageRating_rating_check CHECK ("rating" BETWEEN 1 AND 5)` admits the
domain's thumbs-UP and refuses its thumbs-DOWN. M-G13 is the entry for the
guard that says so before a statement is sent; the alternative — letting the
CHECK raise — reports the same refusal and takes the caller's transaction
with it.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to
sweep unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies
a run with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
THE INTEGRATION SUITES RUN ON A REAL POSTGRESQL, in a container, on the
machine that has a daemon. `governance-rows.test.ts` is the only suite here
that runs without one, and it is the one that reaches the mapping branches a
container suite cannot: a container only ever reads rows THIS binary wrote,
so the legacy-envelope and unknown-vocabulary branches are unreachable from
it except through the two rows the rules suite plants as raw SQL.
EVERY `from` IS A UNIQUE SUBSTRING OF ITS FILE and is applied literally, so a
sweep that silently matched nothing is impossible: the driver refuses an
entry whose `from` occurs zero times or more than once.

mutations.name: M-G09 rows: an ORGANIZATION scope is a relation filter, not an environment one
mutations.from: return { environment: { project: { organizationId: scope.organizationId } } };
mutations.note: An erasure addressed at an organization reaches every environment under it. Narrowed to the organization id as though it were an environment, it reaches nothing at all and a right-to-erasure silently succeeds having erased no rows.

mutations.name: M-G10 safety: the listing is most-recent-first
mutations.from: orderBy: [{ createdAt: "desc" }, { id: "desc" }],
mutations.note: The port's page is a ledger view. Reversed, page one shows the oldest events and an operator watching for a new incident sees the first one ever recorded.

mutations.name: M-G11 safety: the search runs over the TOOL NAME and never over `detail`
mutations.from: : { toolName: { contains: query.search, mode: "insensitive" as const } }),
mutations.to: : { detail: { contains: query.search, mode: "insensitive" as const } }),
mutations.note: The port says so in as many words: `detail` is the one column that can hold whatever a detector saw, and a substring search over it is a way to read it.

mutations.name: M-G12 safety: the search is case-insensitive

mutations.note: Tool names are not normalised anywhere in the schema, so a case-sensitive search finds `web_fetch` and not `WEB_fetch` — the same tool, spelled by a different producer.

mutations.name: M-G14 safety: only rows whose metadata is an ENVELOPE carry a subject

mutations.name: M-G15 safety: anonymising OVERWRITES and never deletes
mutations.note: A compliance ledger that can be emptied is not a compliance ledger. The detector, action, severity and instant must survive the erasure of who it was about.

mutations.note: The revision is the reconciliation key two clients racing a flip converge on. A zero or a value past int4 is refused here rather than by the column.

mutations.name: M-G24 criteria: the duplicate insert does not RAISE

mutations.name: M-G30 criteria: the name pre-check is EXACT, not case-folded
mutations.from:
where: { name, ...scopedWhere(scope) },
          select: CRITERION_COLUMNS,
mutations.to:

mutations.name: M-G31 criteria: removing a criterion DELETES it
mutations.note: The port's `remove` destroys the criterion AND, through `onDelete: Cascade`, every eval taken against it. A soft delete leaves both, and a second `remove` then answers true forever.

mutations.name: M-G42 refusal: the three transaction refusals are RETHROWN, not folded into a Result
mutations.note: `TransactionScopeError` is a DEFECT, not an outcome: a write outside any transaction, with a finished token, or with another live transaction's token. Folded into `GOVERNANCE_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE`, a use case that lost its transaction carries on as though a row had merely failed to write, and the three distinct codes stop being reachable at all.
